newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMANY SAYS SEIZED BEEF IS ILLEGAL BRITISH IMPORT.
newsitem.headline: GERMANY SAYS SEIZED BEEF IS ILLEGAL BRITISH IMPORT.

text.p: German prosecutors on Wednesday confirmed that 172 tonnes of frozen beef seized two weeks ago was British meat exported in defiance of a global ban.

Prosecutors in the northern town of Stralsund said the meat was imported via France with Belgian papers, and that they were investigating a south German meat trading firm for trying to ship it to Russia via the German Baltic island of Ruegen.
A prosecutors' spokesman said the company would be accused of breaking the European Union ban on British beef and other German food hygiene laws.

The export ban was imposed in March 1996 after the British government admitted a likely link between bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) or mad cow disease and its deadly human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease.

The European Commission set alarm bells ringing earlier this month when it said 1,650 tonnes of British beef had been exported illegally via the Netherlands, Germany and possibly France bound for Bosnia-Herzegovina, Poland, Equatorial Guinea, Egypt and Russia.
